plan.english: "Where is my father?" "Your father went to the hill, and the dog followed him. When the sun sets, he will arrive, and we shall eat together." "I am thirsty. Give me water!" "Drink, Swift One, and grow strong." "I have drunk and become sated." "Now look at the hill. Do you see your father?" "I see him! Come!" "I heard you, and I am coming. The dog runs ahead, and I am driving the sheep." "Have you become tired? Have you become thirsty?" "I have become tired, and I drank water from the stream."

title: The Stranger Asks for a Wife

plan.english: "Guest, who are you, and whose son?" "I am the son of a shepherd. My father guards sheep. My name is famous, and I am a free man." "What do you seek in my household?" "I seek a wife. I shall give a bride price of ten cattle, and I shall bring silver and wool." "Your fame has reached me. Sit down and sip the beer. Then we shall speak words, and I shall listen to you." "She is not inside; she went to the river." "I shall sit there." "Do you work? Do you plough?" "I work, and I plough."

"Brother, wake up! Dawn has become bright." "I am awake, and I tremble. In a dream I saw a snake. It crept toward our household." "Do not be afraid, brother. A dream does not kill." "I trust you, and my heart is trembling." "Stand up, and put on your wool. Let us two go to the stream and drink." "If the snake comes, I shall overpower it." "You have become strong, brother, and you are not afraid." "A snake gives a sign. Let us two go to the hill and look."

"Son-in-law, you have arrived! Enter my household, and sit down." "Father-in-law, I bring you wine, and I give wool to your wife." "Wine is dear to us. You are my son-in-law, and my heart is glad." "Where is your wife?" "She is cooking the lamb, and she heard your words." "Where are your two horses?" "They stand in the enclosure, and they have drunk water." "Let us drink and be joyful." "The night has become cold." "Who is this man?" "This is my brother." "And who is that one yonder?" "That is my father-in-law."

"Daughter-in-law, come. I am your husband's mother." "I am afraid." "Do not be afraid, daughter-in-law. This household is dear to you, and I shall protect you. Your husband is dear to us, and he will love you." "I have become cold." "I shall clothe you in wool. Take this ornament, and wear it." "I have heard your words, and I am glad. I shall love you." "Look at that field yonder and at that hill yonder. Your husband ploughs." "I shall work." "Who is that one yonder?" "That is your husband's brother."

"Where were you? I was seeking you." "I was at the river, and I saw a beast in the marsh." "Are you afraid?" "I am not afraid. The beast fled." "Do not go to the marsh again." "Mother was crying out for you. Come, let us two go home. Mother is heating the water. Drink, and be sated." "I am content, brother, and I love you." Then mother came and said: "You two are alive! Come, eat."

"Swift One, yoke the cattle and bring the plough." "How shall I plough?" "Plough the field, and the field will nourish us. Make the path straight, and pull the plough." "I am working." "Look at the field! Your work is good. Now cut the tree, and split it." "I shall cut it, and then I shall build an enclosure for the sheep." "You are working. Sit down by the tree, and sip water."

"Brother-in-law, I married your sister. I shall protect her and love her. She is my heart." "If you deceive her, I shall kill you." "I have heard your words. Be dear to us. May Perkwunos protect us two." "Come, drink wine." "I give you these sheep. Look at them!" "I see them, and my heart is glad." "Eat the lamb, brother-in-law, and be sated." "Who is this man?" "He is my father-in-law, and that one is my brother."

"Swift One, whom do you love?" "I love that one, who dwells at the river. Her father is a shepherd." "Does she love you?" "I do not know." "Then seek her, and speak. She will hear." "I shall go to the river and speak to her father." "Take a good lamb and silver. Say your name, and he will hear it. Your name is famous." "I am afraid." "Do not tremble." "I shall bring her an ornament."

"I give ten cattle, I deliver a hundred sheep, and I carry silver." "This bride price is great. I take it, and I give you this woman. Let the gods hear our pledge, and let Sky see it. If I deceive you, may a wolf seize me. If you deceive me, may a wolf seize you." "The king is listening to our pledge. Then it is great." "Let the pledge stand, and let the bride price be good." "Let the cook set out the lamb, and let us drink wine." "Let there be song."

"The guests are coming." "Arrange the enclosure, and I shall kill a lamb. Let the cook cook it. It is getting dark. Let the fire burn." "Who is coming?" "The king is coming, and the queen is with him." "Then let us give them wine and beer, and let the song be good." "Sit down. The work has succeeded." "I have become tired, and I am glad. They will be sated." "Bring the wine, daughter-in-law. Bring the beer, son-in-law." "Who is this woman?" "This is my daughter-in-law, and that one yonder is my son-in-law."

"The night is coming, and I tremble." "Do not be afraid. The dog guards the enclosure. Lie down, and listen to my song." "What stands?" "The tree stands." "What runs?" "The stream runs." "What burns?" "The fire burns." "What grows?" "The rye grows." "Who dies?" "The mortal dies. The god does not die." "I am listening. Is the snake near?" "The snake is not creeping." "May a good dream come to you. Dawn will become bright, and you will see the sun." "The duck lies flat on the water, the snake lies flat, and the beast is far off."

"Husband, the night has become cold." "Come near, my heart. I shall clothe you in wool." "Do you love me?" "I love you. You are my husband. I shall protect you." "Let us two build a house of our own, and let us plough the field." "May the field be broad. May our name be famous, and may we have two sons." "May we two live."

"Who is Mother Earth?" "The Earth is the mother of mortals. She nourishes them, and Sky is their father." "Where is the sky?" "Sky is above, and Earth is below." "Does the sky hear us?" "He hears and sees." "I shall speak." "Speak, and he will hear." "Who is Perkwunos?" "Perkwunos is a god. When he comes, it rains, and the earth is wet." "Is the sun a god?" "The sun brings light and warms the earth."

In the night a son was born. Dawn became bright. Then the mother looked at him and became glad. Then the father said to her: "A son has been born to you. You are dear to me." Then the father set a name for him. "May this name be famous, and may he have imperishable fame. May his stature be great, and may his strength grow. May he grow, and become strong, and may Dawn protect him." Then the sister came, saw him, and said: "He is dear to me. I shall love him." Then the father laid him down.

"If a guest comes to you, seat him, and give him water and beer. Do not deceive a guest. A guest is dear to the gods." "I have heard you, and I remember." "And if he is hostile?" "Speak friendly words to him. The gods see him." "I shall seat the guest." "You will be a good man, and your name will be famous."

title: The Two Sisters by the Fire

plan.english: The two sisters were sitting by the fire, and it rained. "I am afraid." "Do not be afraid. Mother is near, and the dog is lying flat. Let us two lie down." Then the two lay down, and a dream came to them. Then dawn became bright, and the two stood up. Then the two went to the stream, and they carried water. Then the mother came and covered the sisters with wool. "Lie still." Then the brother came and said: "Where were you two?" "We two were at the stream. We carried water."

"Where are our two sons?" "They went to the river and drove the sheep. When the sun sets, they will both arrive." "Do not be afraid. The wolf does not come to the enclosure." "I see the two of them on the hill, and they are carrying water." "Let us arrange the beer for them." Then the two arrived. "Father!" "Mother!" "We two are thirsty." "Drink, and eat." "At the marsh we saw a beast, and we were not afraid. We overpowered it." "You two have become strong, and your fame is great."

The mother was sitting by the path, and she was looking. "Will my son come?" The sun set, and night was coming. She was afraid. Then she saw a man on the path. Then she recognized him, and cried out, and ran forward. "You have arrived!" Then she became glad. "Where were you?" "I drove the sheep to the hill, and a beast crept toward us. I killed it." "Sit down and sip the beer, and speak to me." "I saw the king, and he gave me silver."

Two brothers drove the sheep to the hill. Then the two saw a wolf, and it crept toward them. "Brother, protect them!" "I shall overpower the wolf." Then the two killed the wolf and became joyful. Then the body of the wolf lay in the field. Then the two ran home. Then the mother gave them water. Then the father said: "Great is your fame. I shall give you two a reward." Then the two brothers sat down and ate the lamb.

Dawn became bright. Then the father cut the wood, and the brother split it. Then the mother heated the water, and the sister dried the wool. Then the horse pulled the plough, and the cattle drank at the stream. "Where are you going?" "I am going to the field." The day became warm. Then the father called: "Come, eat!" Then they sat down.

"Hear my words. I remember. I caught sight of your mother at the river. I got to know her: she was my desire, and I loved her. Then I gave a hundred sheep and ten cattle. Then my father-in-law gave her to me. We two live together, and you were born. Your mother is good." "Did mother love you?" "She loved me, and I love her." "I trust her, and she trusts me." "I built this house."

"Protect your sister, and love her. Take the dog along. The dog is a friend, and he is swift." "I protect her. My sister is dear to me. I love you." "I fear the wolf, brother." "May the wolf not seize you two." "May Sky protect you two. May you two grow strong." Then the mother said: "You two are my heart. I love you two."

The father gave libated wine to the gods. "Gods, drink! Hear our words." Then he gave water to the brother, and he drank and became sated. Then the mother spoke a song of praise: "Father Sky, hear our song, and protect us." Sky heard, and Earth heard. Then the father said: "Remember the gods." Then the brother spoke a song.

The father had three sons. Then he said: "Who will guard the cattle?" "I shall guard them." "I shall plough the field." "I shall go, and I shall seek a wife." Then the father became glad. Then he gave them a dog, a plough, and silver. "You are brothers. Stand together, and do not break the yoke." "Go, and come again."

Dear is the sister to the brother, and dear is the brother to the sister. The one who hears his own father's word is famous. A brother is not a stranger. Work is good. A king is a mortal, and a god is immortal. Blood is red. The mortal dies. Fame is imperishable. Love is great. The wife is the heart of the household. The stream runs, the tree stands, and the hill stands. The beast flees, and the snake creeps.

"Go. May the gods lead you. Do not go astray. Remember your name; remember father and mother. Wear the wool, and take the silver. Do not walk in the night." "I shall go, and I shall come again. I shall remember your words." "May your road be broad. May no wolf seize you. May the day become bright for you." Then the sister said: "Brother, remember your sister." "My body has grown strong, and my heart is content."

Father Sky! Mother Earth! Now hear us. Give this wife fame. May she live; may sons be born to her. "I give her to you, son-in-law." "Father-in-law, I shall indeed love her." Now may fire and water protect her. May the rye grow; may the tree stand. Now may the stream run, and may the hill stand firm. Now may the marsh dry up, and may the snake not creep. May the beast flee; may the locust not eat your rye. May the day become bright, and may the night become warm. May love be between you, and may your desire be great. May your body grow strong; may your youth become bright. May the light be yours; may you two be watchful. May your strength grow; may the giver give you a reward. May your song of praise be heard; may your song be heard.

title: The Bride Leaves Her Father's House

plan.english: Now dawn became bright. Then the father yoked the two horses. The dear mother dressed the one who was marrying. The father led her out; the brother followed. Then she was sweating, and she was trembling; she went. The mother cried out: "Remember me, and come again. Go with fame. Do not be afraid." The father said: "May Sky protect you." And then the two swift horses ran along the path. Then the mother stood; she looked on.

Father Sky, giver of good things! Hear our words, you who yoked the swift horses, you who drove on the wheel of the sun, you who indeed placed the sun, you who overpowered the serpent, you who freed the water, and you who made the earth stand: now hear! Father, give the two of them silver and cattle. Now may the wheel of the sun go forward. May the two horses indeed carry them. Dawn! Come, bring light! Dawn! Become bright for them. May the fire not go out. Now may their name be famous, and may they have great fame. Father, give them imperishable fame. Give love; may the king and the queen live. May the good shepherd be watchful.

"We have arrived. Now we seek a wife for our brother." "Who is your brother? Well, is he a virile man?" "He possesses a hundred cows; he is a free man." "Then enter, guests, and sit down. If you give a bride price, then we shall give her. We shall give ten cattle and a hundred sheep, and we carry silver and wool for you. Lay them down, guests. She is dear to us, and she is our heart. Now protect her, and she will nourish you. Let her come out. Look: she is a light." "Now let this pledge be between us." "The shepherd saw her at the river." "Who are these many men?" "These are indeed my dear brothers."

The father, listening to the guests, led them inside. Then the mother set out the beer; they sat down. Then the father said: "What do you seek?" "We seek a wife for our brother." "Give the bride price, and take her." They gave the bride price; the father took it. Then she brought wool, silver, a yoke; she brought a plough, two horses, ten cattle. The mother said: "Protect her; do not deceive her." Then they drank good beer and were sated. "Dear father-in-law, and son-in-law!"

Now the two swift horses arrived. Then the husband's mother saw the daughter-in-law; she became glad. "Daughter-in-law, come inside to us. May our fire indeed be dear to you." Then the husband's brother brought wine. "Now sit down, daughter-in-law, and drink it." The husband's mother gave the daughter-in-law an ornament. "Now take it, and wear it." The daughter-in-law said: "I bring wool and silver. I am your daughter-in-law. I shall love you." "Daughter-in-law!" "Husband's brother!"

"I marry you; do you take me?" "I marry you, and I take you." "Let us two live together, and let us eat. Now let us two drink wine." "I shall protect you." "I shall love you." "Now let us two go around the fire." "May the fire hear us; may we two not go apart." "Now let the wheel of the sun see our pledge. Let Mother Earth hear it." Then the daughter-in-law's brother said: "I have heard." Then the husband's brother said: "I have seen." Then the mother said: "I am satisfied." "Now, daughter-in-law, son-in-law, husband's brother, and wife's brother: you, indeed, hear our pledge!"

It was getting dark; the guests arrived; the cook was cooking. Then the king and the queen arrived, and the two sat down. "Now who is this man, and who is that one yonder?" "This is the husband's brother; that is the wife's brother." The father gave wine to them. They ate the lamb; they drank wine, and they drank beer, and they spoke a song. Then the cook was content; the shepherd spoke a song of praise. Then the king said: "Now this household is dear to me. May your fame be great, son-in-law." Then the two brothers spoke a song of praise. Then the daughter-in-law's brother stood up and said: "Be content!" Then the night became cold. Then they lay down inside.

title: Prayer to Mother Earth for the Bride

plan.english: Broad Earth, our mother! You who nourish cattle and mortals! Give this one many sons; may she grow strong. You who nourish the rye, the tree, hear us! Now may the wolf not seize the sheep. Now may the beast not enter our enclosure. May the locust indeed not eat the rye. May no one steal the lamb, and may it not die. May the horse indeed not break the yoke. May the water not swell, and may she live.

"You are the mistress of the household, and I am the man." "Enter." "I enter. I shall carry you in. Do not slip." "I am not afraid. My body has grown strong, and my great heart is content." "Your fire is my fire, and your name is my name." "Now I have heard your words; you are indeed dear to me." Then she stood up, and the fire shone. Then the husband's mother said: "This is my brother, and this is my mother." "Now, brother-in-law and father-in-law!"

title: The Husband's Brother Greets the Bride

plan.english: "I am a husband's brother to you; I shall indeed be a brother to you." "I am indeed content, husband's brother. Now where is my husband?" "He is leading the horses. He will come." Then the husband's brother and the wife's brother sat down. "Look at this field and at that hill yonder. Now, daughter-in-law, you will become accustomed to us." "This is my wife's brother; that one yonder is my father-in-law." "Come, brother."

Swift are the horses; he is a virile man, and she is a light. Their splendor is imperishable; love is great. Now, beloved dawn! Imperishable fame indeed! The husband's brother speaks, the wife's brother speaks; the father-in-law speaks, the son-in-law speaks.

"You have married; now protect your wife, and love her. Do not deceive her. Now your father-in-law gave her to you. Plough the field; guard the cattle." "Now I hear you, and I remember." "Now be a friend to your brother-in-law, and he will be a friend to you. Now may the Earth give you two many sons." The father-in-law said: "You are my son-in-law, and I am your father-in-law. Let us drink together." "Father-in-law, son-in-law, brother-in-law: hear us!"
